newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta banking activity rises in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Malta banking activity rises in Q2.

text.p: The consolidated balance sheet of deposit money banks in Malta rose by 4.6 percent in the second quarter of this year, after one percent growth in the first quarter, the Malta Central Bank said in the latest issue of its Quarterly Review. The expansion was slightly higher than the 4.2 percent growth during the second quarter of 1995.
Residents' deposits rose Lm33.2 million ($107m) to Lm1,398.8 million.

Demand deposits rose by Lm11.1 million or 15.1 percent but the Central Bank said a substantial amount of this growth happened when a category of savings deposits offered by one bank were re-classified after they were made available for payments by cheque.
This re-classifiction was also partly responsible for a drop in savings deposits, which were down three percent to Lm502.8 million after showing some growth in the previous quarter.

The Central Bank said depositors had shown a preference for time deposits, particularly in view of higher nominal interest rates offered since March. Time deposits expanded by Lm37.5 million or 4.9 percent to Lm811.2million, the largest quarterly increase since the first quarter of 1995.

The increase in residents' deposits occured entirely in named deposits in Maltese liri. Foreign currency deposits, which had increased by 2.4 percent in the first quarter, fell by 1.2 percent to Lm148.1 million in the second quarter, reflecting a combination of the downward trend in international interest rates coupled with an increase in domestic rates.
Bearer deposits rose 6.6 percent to Lm43.7 million.
The deposit money banks' liabilities to non-residents rose by 17.0 percent to Lm194.2 million due to fresh short-term borrowing by one bank in April.
The banks' other liabilities rose by 9.0 percent to Lm307.4 million, mostly due to increased deposits from offshore subsidiaries.

Local lending rose by Lm25.1 million to Lm1,017.5 million, the smallest increase since the second quarter of 1994. Local investments, mostly treasury bills, rose by Lm20.6 million or 8.4 percent to Lm265.2 million, considerably higher than the 4.4 percent growth in the first quarter.
The deposit money banks' foreign assets rose by 3.4 percent to Lm525.2 million after having fallen by 8.9 percent during the first quarter.
The deposit money banks' reserves, mostly cash holdings and deposits with the Central Bank, rose by 1.7 percent to Lm117.5 million. ($1=Lm0.35)
